subject: Mutual Action Plan: Technical gating, benchmarks & model shortlist
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Evan Liu <evan.liu@healthgrid.com>; Priya Singh <psingh@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Mutual Action Plan: technical gating, benchmarks & model shortlist (post-call recap)

Hi Evan / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum toward the November procurement window: 

1) Technical milestone (our immediate MAP item): HealthGrid technical evaluation engineering runbook and acceptance criteria. We propose a 3-week bench+integration sprint focused on latency, cost-per-token, and a functional accuracy slate.

2) Model shortlist for the trial: a mix of open and quantized variants — we recommend: Llama-3-70B (q4), Mistral-Instruct-Chat (16k), and Redwood-1-small (fp16) as a fallback. We’ll provide image/embedding parity notes for HealthGrid’s summary use cases.

3) Bench targets: 95th-percentile inference latency <= 250ms for typical 120-token responses (p95), and token unit cost <= $0.0009 under steady-state when batched to 8. We'll instrument runs to show trade-offs.

4) Dependencies: access to a representative prompt set (anonymized production slices), a test dataset for redaction checks, and a secure S3 location for our runner to upload KV-cache traces.

Action items / owners I captured:
- HealthGrid: provide prompt corpus + procurement point-of-contact (Priya to confirm). Target: 2026-11-02.
- Redwood (Sergio / Marissa): deliver MAP draft with milestone dates and resource roster. Target: 2026-11-06.
- Redwood (Karthik): produce benchmark spec and runner configuration for the shortlisted models. Target: 2026-11-09.

I attached a first-pass MAP spreadsheet that lays out milestones, owners, and acceptance criteria. If that aligns, we’ll formalize dates and schedule a 30-min tech kickoff next week.

Attachments: MAP_v1_tech_milestones.xlsx, latency_benchmark-specs.pdf

Thanks —
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

--
From: Evan Liu <evan.liu@healthgrid.com>

Cc: Priya Singh <psingh@healthgrid.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: technical gating, benchmarks & model shortlist (post-call recap)

Sergio —

Thanks for the clear recap. That aligns with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Prompt corpus: we'll provide 1k anonymized prompts by COB Monday (2026-11-01). They will include a short/long split and a few structured-output examples.
- Procurement: looping in procurement inbox (procurement@healthgrid.com) — they'll need a high-level SOW and the typical vendor questionnaire.
- Acceptance criteria: the latency target looks reasonable as a starting point; can you include a fallback SLA if p95 spikes above 400ms during load tests? We want an operational contingency.

Also — can you confirm whether Redwood can run the benchmark within our VPC (preferred) or will this be hosted by Redwood? We have data residency constraints for logs.

Thanks — Evan
Evan Liu
Head of Platform Engineering | HealthGrid
evan.liu@healthgrid.com

Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: technical gating, benchmarks & model shortlist (post-call recap)

Evan —

Appreciate the quick confirmation. Short answers to your questions and updated commitments on our side: 

1) VPC execution: Redwood can run the benchmark inside HealthGrid's VPC using our Private deployment runner (we'll need the temporary IAM role and an s3 write bucket with restricted permissions). Karthik and I will own the onboarding steps.

2) Fallback SLA: we will add a contingency line to the MAP: if p95 > 400ms for two consecutive business days during benchmark runs, Redwood will (a) open an incident, (b) run a compacted quantized variant (q4) as an automatic fallback, and (c) provide a regression report plus remediation plan within 24 hours.

3) Deliverables and dates (updated):
- 2026-11-06: MAP_v1 with milestone dates and resource contacts (Sergio / Marissa).
- 2026-11-09: Benchmark spec + runner config (Karthik).
- 2026-11-16: First within-VPC bench run with HealthGrid prompt corpus (Redwood eng ops).

I've attached a short runner checklist and a sample IAM policy stub to accelerate your security team review. Let us know if procurement needs additional compliance artifacts (SOC2, DPA).

Attachments: latency_benchmark-specs.pdf

Best,
Marissa

Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: technical gating, benchmarks & model shortlist (post-call recap)

Hi Sergio / Marissa —

Thanks for the updates. We received the anonymized prompt corpus yesterday and the procurement team is ready to accept the MAP draft. Two small asks before you finalize the spreadsheet: 

1) Can you add a column in the MAP that maps each milestone to a specific success metric (e.g., p95 latency, token cost per 1k tokens, functional accuracy measured by exact-match on the 50 critical prompts)? That will make it easier for procurement and engineering to sign off.

2) Please include an explicit data-handling row that lists what telemetry Redwood will collect (latency percentiles, token counts, anonymized traces) and how long you will retain those logs. Our security policy requires retention <= 90 days for benchmark traces unless otherwise approved.

Assuming those two items are added, HealthGrid confirms target close date of 2026-11-30 and procurement will issue an initial PO contingent on successful bench results.

Thanks —
Priya
Priya Singh
Senior Procurement Manager | HealthGrid
